question: On the same lamp robot, does routing touch/approach events through an artificial hormone (AHM) that modulates the SO(2) CPG nod rhythm and the emotion transitions change (1) the source-to-physical response latency and (2) the emotion switching rate during a 600 s human play scenario, compared with the direct fixed-rule FSM of Lab06?
hypothesis: If the hormone path C1 is used instead of the direct FSM C0, then emotion switching rate per minute decreases (fewer brief flips under noisy approach/near input) while the median both-onset latency stays below 1 s (expected increase < 0.2 s), because H integrates production and clearance over seconds and the receptor output changes phi gradually. Boundary: the claim covers this lamp, these parameters and scripted interaction only; it does not claim the robot feels emotion.
biological_inspiration_source: Neurohormonal modulation of central pattern generators: slow neuromodulators (e.g. octopamine/serotonin in insects) change the frequency and gain of rhythmic motor circuits instead of commanding muscles directly. Abstracted as the Artificial Hormone Mechanism of Homchanthanakul et al. (2019, IROS, DOI 10.1109/IROS40897.2019.8968580) and the hormone-CPG architecture of Ngamkajornwiwat et al. (2020, IEEE Access 8, DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2020.2992794). Mechanism used: production by a stimulus, clearance by decay, binding by receptor activity, receptor output as bounded modulator.
AHM_equation: Source (Homchanthanakul et al. 2019 via Week04): Hc(t) = beta*Hc(t-1) + Hg(t) - Hr(t), Hg = alpha_h*f(S), Hr = sum(gamma_i*Receptor_i). Proposed course model used (one hormone, 'arousal' H): H_raw = H + dt*(k_prod*S - k_clear*H - k_bind*R), H = clamp(H_raw,0,1), R = clamp((H - H_min)/(H_max - H_min),0,1), S = 1 for a recognized touch/button/approach in the tick, else 0.
SO2_CPG_equation: Dr. Poramate Manoonpong SO(2) CPG (lec5 slide 18, Lab03): a1(t+1) = alpha*[cos(phi)*o1(t) + sin(phi)*o2(t)], a2(t+1) = alpha*[-sin(phi)*o1(t) + cos(phi)*o2(t)], oi(t+1) = tanh(ai(t+1)), simultaneous update, alpha = 1.10, initial (o1,o2) = (0.10,0), sigma = tanh is the course-lab convention.
integration_description: AHM-CPG and AHM-emotion: R modulates the CPG phase increment phi = clamp(0.20 + 0.20*R, 0.10, 0.45) rad, and o1 scaled to the nod axis (nod_amplitude 0.18 rad) gives the rhythmic happy/interested expression; the emotion FSM uses R with hysteresis (enter interested/happy when R >= 0.30, leave when R <= 0.15) instead of a fixed 2 s timeout. near/clear/fault safety transitions bypass the hormone in both conditions.
independent_variable: Controller path: C0 direct fixed-rule FSM (Lab06 baseline policy, fixed phi = 0.20 rad nod rhythm, 2 s timeout) vs C1 hormone path (same sensors, poses, RGB, safety rules; AHM drives phi and active-state exit).

conditions.name: C0
conditions.change: Direct Lab06 baseline FSM; fixed phi = 0.20 rad; interested/happy exit by 2 s timeout; no hormone state

conditions.name: C1
conditions.change: Hormone path: k_prod 0.8 /s, k_clear 0.6 /s, k_bind 0.2 /s; R modulates phi and active-state exit; everything else identical to C0

metrics.name: both_onset_latency
metrics.measurement: max(first servo motion onset, first LED colour onset) minus button/touch press time (or distance threshold crossing); press marked by a contact switch LED and onsets by a 240 fps camera + photodiode on the LED, all in one video timeline; simulation uses the virtual applied-command onset
metrics.missing_rule: no onset within the scenario window = missing (null, counted in the denominator as a miss), never 0; >1 s with onset = deadline fail reported separately

metrics.name: emotion_switching_rate
metrics.measurement: count of /lamp/emotion changes between consecutive messages in the rosbag over the 600 s scenario divided by 10 min; flips shorter than 0.2 s reported separately
metrics.missing_rule: if the bag has a gap > 0.5 s the gap duration is excluded from the denominator and the trial is flagged; trials stopped early are kept and reported with their actual duration

metrics.name: nod_frequency
metrics.measurement: rising zero crossings of the commanded nod angle in happy/interested segments (simulation and /lamp/servo_command), checked against servo encoder or video on the robot
metrics.missing_rule: segments with fewer than 2 crossings are N/A and listed

controls: Same student_policy.py transition table, poses, RGB, bounds and slew limit in C0 and C1; policy SHA-256 recorded per trial
Same scripted 600 s interaction schedule (time-stamped task cards) and the same synthetic input traces/seeds 41-43 in simulation
Same lamp hardware, servo calibration file, ToF sensor mounting, room lighting and table position; firmware and ROS 2 Jazzy package versions frozen during trials

parameters.name: R_emotion_hysteresis
parameters.provenance: group proposed value; to be tuned in simulation before robot trials and then frozen

parameters.name: max_slew
parameters.provenance: Lab06 bound; real robot implemented with measured elapsed time

parameters.name: joint_bounds
parameters.provenance: Lab06 semantic bounds; to be mapped to servo angles by calibration

simulation_plan: ROS 2 Jazzy on Ubuntu 24.04: synthetic_inputs (or replayed traces) -> interaction + new ahm_node + so2_cpg_node -> output_collector, seven /lamp topics plus a versioned /lamp/hormone_r topic; every node writes a perf_counter_ns sidecar log; rosbag2 records all /lamp topics; 3 seeds x C0/C1 on the 22 s protocol and 3 x C0/C1 on a 600 s scripted trace; offline_lab.py used first to validate metrics.
real_robot_plan: ESP32 micro-ROS client reads ToF distance (m), capacitive touch pad and push button and drives 3 hobby servos and an RGB LED; micro-ROS Agent over serial on the host. Calibration before trials: neutral pose, direction and rad-to-servo mapping per axis with a protractor, bounds checked at low speed, LED colour check; physical onset measured with a 240 fps camera and a photodiode on the LED.
clock_correlation_plan: ESP32 adds a local sequence number per sensor sample in a sidecar debug topic (not in the 7 contract messages) and blinks the LED at power-up; host logs receipt perf_counter_ns per sequence; the camera sees both the operator's press indicator and the LED/servo, so source and physical onset share one video clock; error bound = 1 frame (4.2 ms) + photodiode rise time, reported with every latency.
safety_stop_plan: Operator holds a hardware e-stop that cuts servo power; software watchdog: stale input > 0.12 s or invalid value -> neutral pose; near (< 0.20 m) -> afraid retreat pose; servo torque limited by current-limited supply; participant keeps hands away from linkages; trial stops on any unexpected motion, servo stall or participant request, and the log is kept with the reason.
order_counterbalancing: Per participant/repeat the condition order alternates ABBA: repeat 1 C0 then C1, repeat 2 C1 then C0, repeat 3 C0 then C1; robot state, hormone H and CPG state are reset and the lamp returns to neutral between trials.
paired_seed_or_participant_plan: Simulation: seeds 41/42/43 paired across C0/C1. Robot: 3 participants, each does C0 and C1 with the same task card; informed consent and the right to stop are explained before the session; no personal data beyond an anonymous ID is stored.
expected_input_ids_before_run: 22 s protocol: baseline primary 7 IDs button_01, touch_01, approach_01, clear_01, near_01, clear_02, button_02 (all 10 sources kept). 600 s scenario: every scripted press/touch/approach/near/clear card is an expected input, declared in the task card before the session.
timeline: 2026-11-18 implement ahm_node and so2_cpg_node and pass offline checks; 2026-11-25 ROS 2 simulation trials C0/C1 x 3; 2026-12-02 ESP32/micro-ROS bring-up and calibration; 2026-12-09 robot trials C0/C1 x 3 with 600 s scenario; 2026-12-16 analysis and report.
